title: SlimFaas
caption: A greener way to run agent tools on Kubernetes.
voice: Meet SlimFaas! This CNCF Sandbox project lets idle agent tools scale to zero for greener Kubernetes workloads. Keep your existing HTTP app and call it directly, in any language. No special driver needed!

title: Synchronous functions
caption: Call a sleeping service and get the result in the same HTTP response.
voice: First up: synchronous functions over HTTP. Let's wake one up!

title: Start with zero replicas
caption: The HTTP route is available while the function sleeps.
voice: Find Fibonacci on the right. Zero ready replicas. Its HTTP address is already available.

title: One HTTP request wakes one pod
caption: The caller waits for Kubernetes to make the replica ready.
voice: Send the call. See that dot? Kubernetes starts a pod, SlimFaas forwards the request, and the caller gets fifty-five.

title: Back to zero
caption: The deployment releases its worker after the idle timeout.
voice: Now watch the idle timer. The last pod goes to sleep, ready for the next call.

title: Asynchronous queues
caption: Accept the burst now. Process it as workers become ready.
voice: Next up: asynchronous queues over HTTP. Here comes the burst!

title: Thirty HTTP requests arrive together
caption: HTTP 202 means the work has entered the queue.
voice: Thirty HTTP requests ask for Fibonacci of forty-eight. All thirty get an accepted response while the work waits in the queue.

title: Four workers share the backlog
caption: Each worker takes one calculation at a time.
voice: The backlog wakes more pods. Four workers each take one calculation at a time, keeping CPU demand under control.

title: Let the queue absorb the spike
caption: 30 completed calculations. The deployment returns to zero.
voice: The queue gives Kubernetes time to scale. All thirty calculations finish. With the backlog empty, the workers return to zero.

title: Publish / subscribe
caption: Tell every ready subscriber when a shared tool definition changes.
voice: Publish and subscribe over HTTP: one event for every replica!

title: Four replicas, four local caches
caption: Each evaluator and audit pod caches the tool catalog.
voice: Our agent system has two evaluators and two audit pods. Each keeps its own tool catalog. A tool has just changed.

title: One HTTP event reaches all four pods
caption: Each replica invalidates its own cached copy.
voice: Publish once. Follow those paths! All four pods receive the HTTP event and discard their stale copy.

title: Durable Streams
caption: Let each subscribed function track its own progress.
voice: Now let's pass an agent result through a durable Stream over HTTP.

title: One result, two subscriptions
caption: Workers within a function share its subscription.
voice: One HTTP append gives the evaluator and the audit function their own copy to process. Each function tracks its own progress.

title: One replica per function, per attempt
caption: Both functions acknowledge sequence 1. Both show zero lag.
voice: One replica per function handles this attempt. Both subscriptions acknowledge sequence one, with zero lag. Retries are possible, so make handlers safe to repeat.

title: Jobs & schedules
caption: Queue batch work and schedule it for later.
voice: There's more! Submit a job over HTTP or by cron. SlimFaas queues runs until a slot opens. You can also schedule a function to wake before the morning rush.
card: Extra runs wait for an available slot.

title: Sets
caption: Cache small values by key over HTTP.
voice: Cache a tool result with Sets. Post a value under a key over HTTP, set its expiry, then read it back on the next call.
card: This cache entry expires after one minute.

title: Files
caption: Stream temporary artifacts by key over HTTP.
voice: With Files, stream bytes in over HTTP and pass the key to the next agent. A few kilobytes or hundreds of megabytes? Same route! Stream the artifact back before it expires.
card: Pass the key between agents. Stream the bytes on demand.

title: Try SlimFaas
caption: Bring an HTTP tool. Watch its first pod wake up.
voice: Give the local demo a spin and watch your own HTTP tool wake up!
